This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Airlines are working to get schedules back on track
following the nationwide ground stop
that disrupted Travel Friday.
Federal aviation officials expect operations
to return to normal by the end of today,
but passengers at airports across the country
are still trying to make their way home.
Chaka Masayo was stranded at Newark Liberty

- Investigators are still working to determine
how maintenance on an air traffic control network
triggered such a widespread failure.

is placing the blame on a longtime FAA contractor.
- L3 Harris Technology.
They say the company was doing a routine maintenance upgrade

Sean Duffy and FAA leaders were asked several times

A federal judge has temporarily blocked President Trump's
plans to redevelop a public park and golf course
along the Potomac River in Washington, D.C.
and PR's Kate Bartlett reports.
- The judge on Saturday ordered a two week delay
to any work on the site which had been due to close
on Sunday for 15 months while it was redeveloped.
Trump, an avid golfer, wants to turn the historic site,
East Potomac Golf Links,
into a championship level golf course.
The plaintiffs in the case,
including the D.C. Preservation League,
argue the new course would be unaffordable.
On Saturday, before the order, Trump said on social media
that anyone in the D.C. area would be given a 50% discount.
Kate Bartlett, NPR News.
- A crowd celebrated as SpaceX
brought one of its Starship rockets safely back from orbit
and PR's Jeff Fromfield reports the spacecraft
returned to the same launch pad left a day earlier.
- Starship re-entered Earth's atmosphere
and swooped over the Baja Peninsula.
It crossed Texas to the same pad
it took off from on the Gulf Coast.
Starship burst through low clouds
and then lowered itself onto the pad
where it was grabbed by giant mechanical arms.
- I still can't believe what we just saw.
That was insane.
That was wild.
Picture perfect.
- The landing is a major breakthrough for SpaceX
which seeks to one day make Starship
a rapidly reusable rocket.
Jeff Fromfield, NPR News.
- This is NPR.
Protesters across Portugal are taking to the streets
over the country's housing crisis.
The demonstrations follow weeks of smaller tent protests
in Lisbon and Porto, some broken up by police using force.
Alison Roberts reports from Lisbon.
- Activists from the camp-ins of recent weeks
were joined by unions and leftist parties
for the largest protests so far
demanding solutions on housing.
Tens of thousands marched in more than 30 cities
including Lisbon and Porto.
The majority of Portuguese own their homes
but a tourism boom and an influx of foreign money
have sent prices soaring.
In Lisbon, average rents now exceed salaries.
The government has reduced tenant protections
saying this will persuade landlords
to put more homes on the market.
The protesters want a different approach
including more public housing.
For NPR News, I'm Alison Roberts in Lisbon.
(singing in foreign language)
- The Philippines has won the first Asian edition
of the Eurovision Song Contest.
19-year-old Carmel took the title Saturday in Bangkok
with her dance pop song, "Sobra Sobra."
The song celebrates female empowerment
and pays tribute to Filipino women.
Artists from 11 countries competed in the final.
Thailand finished second followed by Vietnam in third.
Viewers cast votes from more than 180 countries
and territories around the world.
I'm Windsor Johnston and you're listening to NPR News
from Washington.

topics.text: Airlines work to restore schedules after nationwide ground stop disrupts Friday travel
Investigators examine air traffic control network failure; administration blames L3Harris contractor
Federal judge temporarily blocks Trump plan to redevelop East Potomac Golf Links in Washington
SpaceX Starship returns from orbit and lands back on its Texas launch pad
Protesters across Portugal march over housing crisis, with tens of thousands in Lisbon and Porto
Philippines wins first Asian Eurovision Song Contest in Bangkok with Carmel's 'Sobra Sobra'
